To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

InkTag: (1) is a virtualization based architecture for secure applications on an insecure operating system, (2) introduces paraverification, which simplifies the Inktag hypervisor by forcing an untrusted OS to participate in its verification, (3) uses attribute-based access control to create decentralized access policies, and (4) is the first system of this type to ensure consistency between data and metadata, and therefore recoverability in the event of system crashes.
InkTag is an untrusted OS architecture that gives strong guarantees to high assurance applications by combining paraverification, attribute-based access control, and consistent secure data.
InkTag is the first system that allows secure applications to be run on a malicious operating system with a small trusted computing base.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a virtualization-based operating system that provides strong security guarantees to applications even when the operating system is malicious.
the problem of running secure applications on an insecure operating system.
building a secure system on an untrusted platform.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
InkTag is the first untrusted operating system architecture to provide both a strong safety guarantee and the ability to run high-assurance applications.
InkTag provides the first secure, practical, and usable virtualization-based architecture for untrusted operating systems.
InkTag provides a secure, flexible and efficient platform for high-assurance applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a secure hypervisor for untrusted operating systems, which can securely execute high-assurance applications without the need to trust the operating system.
InkTag allows you to run a secure process without trusting the operating systems, and the secure process can create its own decentralized access control policies.
InkTag provides a secure, recoverable virtualization-based architecture for high-assurance applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
virtualization is not only a useful tool to isolate applications, it is also a tool to enforce safety policies.
a secure hypervisor can provide a high degree of security to a wide variety of applications.
it is feasible to create a system with strong guarantees that can run useful high-assurance applications in an untrusted operating environment.
